title: Measured cmm codebase memory mcp retrieval arm beats naive on the zonoid code nav corpus
summary: Ran the codebase-memory-mcp structural-search arm against the 13-query Phase 1 code-nav corpus (indexed D:/zonoid/lib -> 2063 nodes/4786 edges and D:/zonoid/routes -> 256/473; per query: search_graph name_pattern from query terms, bundle = matched node names+files). Results vs the existing arms: cmm mean_recall 0.506, mean_tokens 327, mean_tokens_per_correct_symbol 170, hit 10/13 queries. naive (grep+read) recall 0.321, tokens 3026, tok/correct 1945, 7/13. subconscious (KB NOT onboarded) recall 0.045, tokens 580, 2/13 (unfair until a code onboard). So cmm gets HIGHER recall at ~1/9 the tokens of naive = ~11x better tokens-per-correct-symbol, and wins exactly on the structural queries naive fails: q01 git worktree (cmm 1.0 vs naive 0), q08 merge-abort (cmm 1.0 vs naive 0), q07 overlay status/lease (cmm 1.0). cmm's 0.506 is a LOWER BOUND: the quick arm used only search_graph name-pattern matching; adding get_code_snippet, trace_path for call chains, and semantic_query would raise recall. cmm missed q02/q03/q11 (ask-gate / context-gate symbols crowded out by the 12-result cap). The Phase 1b worker that was meant to persist this DIED on an API error after thrashing to ~489k output tokens / 22M cache-read, writing zero files — root cause: it indexed the full worktree (pulling .graph's thousands of state files); the fix is to scope indexing to code dirs only.
